title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

reading.body:
This is an access-control failure inside a law enforcement deployment. A system built to support police work, the Flock camera network, was queried by an officer who had a personal connection to the person being looked up. The searches were run through Flock and through other restricted state databases, CJIS and CORI, which are meant to be used for official purposes. The failure is not that the system returned wrong information. It is that the system returned correct information to someone who should not have been asking.

The point of failure sits at the query layer, not the camera layer. Nothing in the reporting suggests the technology malfunctioned or that the data was inaccurate. What failed was the assumption that anyone with credentials is asking for a legitimate reason. Catching this kind of misuse requires auditing who searched for whom and comparing those queries against the officer's own connections, which is a review that happens after the fact rather than at the moment of the search. The department only identified the pattern through an internal affairs investigation, which began after the woman came forward.

What is not established is whether Rogers will face criminal charges, whether the complaint filed on July 17 will lead to a conviction, or what the Select Board will decide about his employment. The accusation is an allegation, the criminal complaint is not a verdict, and the internal affairs finding concerns department policy rather than criminal guilt.

reports.title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

summary:
A Stow police officer, Jason Rogers, is accused of misusing police databases to track a woman he previously dated. The woman said she ended the abusive relationship about five years ago and changed her identity, phone number, and social media habits. She discovered this summer that Rogers had searched for her location using the Flock camera system and other law enforcement databases, including CJIS and CORI, multiple times in 2024 and 2025. She also said he drove by her home.

The Stow Police Department filed a criminal complaint against Rogers on July 17 for possible state law violations. After a four-week internal affairs investigation, the department found he used state systems to get information about the woman. Rogers was placed on paid administrative leave in July, then unpaid leave as of July 31. The woman has a restraining order against him lasting at least a year. A Select Board hearing next week could decide his employment status.
